source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר זָקֵ֖ן שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיָּ֧שֶׂם אֶת־בָּנָ֛יו שֹׁפְטִ֖ים לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when was old Samuel, and he made his sons judges over Israel.

en.L: And it happened, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel.
en.B: In his old age Samuel appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
en.R: When Samuel grew old, he made his sons judges to lead Israel.

decisions.choice: judges: leaders who governed Israel and settled its disputes
decisions.reason: The judges of the book of Judges were leaders raised up to rescue and govern Israel (Judges 2:16-18). Samuel himself judged Israel all his life, going round a circuit of towns (7:15-17). Here the word names the same kind of leadership, given to Samuel's sons.

decisions.choice: Samuel was old: he passed his leadership on to his sons
decisions.reason: Judges were raised up one by one, not by inheritance. Gideon refused to found a line of rulers (Judges 8:22-23). By appointing his sons, Samuel makes leadership pass within a family, and his age is the reason the elders give for asking for a king (verse 5).

decisions.choice: judges to lead Israel
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Readable adds "lead" so that "judges" is not taken to mean only judges in a law court.

source.text: וַיְהִ֞י שֶׁם־בְּנ֤וֹ הַבְּכוֹר֙ יוֹאֵ֔ל וְשֵׁ֥ם מִשְׁנֵ֖הוּ אֲבִיָּ֑ה שֹׁפְטִ֖ים בִּבְאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] name of his son the firstborn Joel, and [the] name of his second Abijah; judges in Beersheba.

en.L: And the name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second [was] Abijah; [they were] judges in Beersheba.
en.B: His firstborn son was named Joel, and his second Abijah. They served as judges in Beersheba.
en.R: His oldest son was named Joel, and his second son was Abijah. They were judges in the town of Beersheba.

decisions.choice: Joel and Abijah: names that confess Yahweh
decisions.reason: Joel means "Yahweh is God" and Abijah "Yahweh is my father". The sons bear names of faith, which makes their conduct in verse 3 all the sadder.

decisions.choice: Beersheba: a town in the far south of the land
decisions.reason: Beersheba lay at the southern edge of Israel; "from Dan to Beersheba" means the whole land (3:20). It was far from Ramah, Samuel's home, and from the towns of his own circuit, Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah (7:16-17).

decisions.choice: They served as judges (Balanced); They were judges (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "judges in Beersheba". Balanced and Readable supply a verb to make a full sentence; Readable also says that Beersheba was a town.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־הָלְכ֤וּ בָנָיו֙ בִּדְרָכָ֔יו וַיִּטּ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַבָּ֑צַע וַיִּ֨קְחוּ־שֹׁ֔חַד וַיַּטּ֖וּ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃פ

records.literal_gloss: But not walked his sons in his ways, and they turned aside after the gain, and took a bribe, and turned aside justice.

en.L: But his sons did not walk in his ways, and they turned aside after gain, and took bribes, and turned aside justice.
en.B: But his sons did not follow his ways. They turned aside after dishonest gain; they took bribes and bent justice.
en.R: But Samuel's sons did not live the way their father did. They were greedy for money. They took bribes and made unfair decisions.

decisions.choice: his sons (the reading the scribes marked)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) can be read "his son"; the reading the scribes marked in the margin (qere) is "his sons", which the printed text follows. The plural fits the plural verbs and the two sons named in verse 2, so the meaning is the same either way. Reviewers should check this against the Masoretic notes.

decisions.choice: walk in his ways: live as he lived
decisions.reason: A person's "ways" are the conduct of their life. Samuel ruled honestly and could later call the people to witness that he had taken no bribe (12:3-5); his sons did not follow him.

decisions.choice: took a bribe and turned aside justice: the very things the law forbids judges
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 16:19 tells judges, "You shall not turn aside justice ... and you shall not take a bribe" (see also Exodus 23:6-8). The sons break it word for word. The word for justice here returns in verses 9 and 11 for the "way" of the king.

decisions.choice: gain: profit got dishonestly
decisions.reason: The word means profit, often profit gained by violence or fraud. Moses was told to choose judges who hate such gain (Exodus 18:21).

decisions.choice: bent justice (Balanced); made unfair decisions (Readable)
decisions.reason: To "turn aside justice" is to twist a verdict away from what is right. Balanced keeps a picture close to the Hebrew; Readable says what it meant in practice.

source.text: וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֔וּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הָרָמָֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered themselves all [the] elders of Israel and came to Samuel to Ramah.

en.L: And all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
en.B: So all the elders of Israel came together and went to Samuel at Ramah.
en.R: So all the leaders of Israel met together and went to see Samuel at his home in Ramah.

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the heads of families and clans who spoke for the people
decisions.reason: The elders were senior men who led their clans and acted for the nation as a whole (4:3; Exodus 3:16). Their coming together shows that the request is the people's considered decision, not a passing complaint.

decisions.choice: Ramah: Samuel's home town
decisions.reason: Samuel was born in Ramah (1:1, 19), lived there and built an altar there, and judged Israel from it (7:17).

decisions.choice: leaders; at his home in Ramah
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders", since the word here is about their position, not their age, and adds that Ramah was Samuel's home (see m2).

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּה֙ אַתָּ֣ה זָקַ֔נְתָּ וּבָנֶ֕יךָ לֹ֥א הָלְכ֖וּ בִּדְרָכֶ֑יךָ עַתָּ֗ה שִֽׂימָה־לָּ֥נוּ מֶ֛לֶךְ לְשָׁפְטֵ֖נוּ כְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to him, Look, you are old, and your sons not walk in your ways; now appoint for us a king to judge us like all the nations.

en.L: And they said to him, "Look, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us, like all the nations."
en.B: They said to him, "You are old, and your sons do not follow your ways. So now appoint a king to judge us, as all the nations have."
en.R: They said to him, "You are old now, and your sons do not live the way you do. So choose a king to lead us, just as all the other nations have."

decisions.choice: to judge us: to govern and lead us
decisions.reason: The people use the verb that described the judges' work: to rule, settle disputes and lead in war (verse 20). They ask for the same leadership, but from a king and his line.

decisions.choice: a king like all the nations: the request Deuteronomy foresaw
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 17:14 expects Israel to say, "I will set a king over me, like all the nations that are around me." The law allows a king, but only one whom Yahweh chooses and who lives under the law (Deuteronomy 17:15-20). Israel had been called to be set apart from the nations (Leviticus 20:26; Numbers 23:9); now the elders want to be like them.

decisions.choice: look ... now: the request rests on the facts just stated
decisions.reason: "Look" points to Samuel's age and his sons' conduct; "now" draws the conclusion. The elders present their request as the answer to a real problem.

decisions.choice: Look left out (Balanced, Readable); choose a king to lead us (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Look" here only draws attention, which English does by tone. Readable says "lead" for "judge", as in verse 1, and "choose" for "appoint".

source.text: וַיֵּ֤רַע הַדָּבָר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמְר֔וּ תְּנָה־לָּ֥נוּ מֶ֖לֶךְ לְשָׁפְטֵ֑נוּ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And was evil the thing in [the] eyes of Samuel when they said, Give to us a king to judge us. And prayed Samuel to Yahweh.

en.L: And the thing was evil in the eyes of Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." And Samuel prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: But Samuel was displeased when they said, "Give us a king to judge us," and he prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Samuel did not like it when they said, "Give us a king to lead us." So he prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the thing was evil in the eyes of Samuel: it displeased him
decisions.reason: "Evil in the eyes of" means that someone judged a thing bad. The same words describe what displeases Yahweh (Judges 2:11). Samuel is troubled by the request for a king, not only by the remark about his age.

decisions.choice: give us a king: the request in its barest form
decisions.reason: The narrator repeats the people's words in short, with "give" in place of "appoint" (verse 5). What stays is the core of it: a king, to judge them.

decisions.choice: Samuel prayed: he brought the matter to Yahweh
decisions.reason: Samuel is shown as one who prays for Israel (7:5, 8-9; 12:19, 23). He does not answer the elders himself but waits for Yahweh's word.

decisions.choice: was displeased (Balanced); did not like it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture; Balanced and Readable give its sense in everyday words.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל שְׁמַע֙ בְּק֣וֹל הָעָ֔ם לְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אֹֽתְךָ֙ מָאָ֔סוּ כִּֽי־אֹתִ֥י מָאֲס֖וּ מִמְּלֹ֥ךְ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Samuel, Listen to [the] voice of the people in all that they say to you, for not you they have rejected, but me they have rejected from being king over them.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from being king over them.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Listen to the people in everything they are saying to you. It is not you they have rejected; it is {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they have rejected as their king.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Do what the people are asking you to do. They have not turned away from you. They have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They do not want {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to be their king.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of the people: do what they ask
decisions.reason: To "listen to someone's voice" often means to agree to what they ask (Genesis 21:12). Yahweh tells Samuel to give the people a king; the command comes three times (verses 7, 9, 22).

decisions.choice: they have rejected me from being king over them: Yahweh was Israel's king
decisions.reason: Israel's true king was Yahweh (Exodus 15:18; Deuteronomy 33:5). Gideon refused to rule because "Yahweh will rule over you" (Judges 8:23), and Samuel later says the people asked for a king "when Yahweh your God was your king" (12:12). Wanting a king like the nations is a turning away from Yahweh's rule.

decisions.choice: rejected: refused, cast aside
decisions.reason: The verb means to reject with contempt or refuse. It is used of despising Yahweh's laws (Leviticus 26:15), and later of Yahweh's rejecting Saul when Saul had rejected his word (15:23, 26).

decisions.choice: turned away from; do not want me to be their king
decisions.reason: Readable uses plainer words for "rejected" and makes "from being king over them" its own sentence.

source.text: כְּכָֽל־הַמַּעֲשִׂ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֗וּ מִיּוֹם֩ הַעֲלֹתִ֨י אֹתָ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ וְעַד־הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיַּ֣עַזְבֻ֔נִי וַיַּעַבְד֖וּ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים כֵּ֛ן הֵ֥מָּה עֹשִׂ֖ים גַּם־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: According to all the deeds which they have done from the day I brought up them from Egypt and until this day, and they have forsaken me and served other gods, so they [are] doing also to you.

en.L: According to all the deeds that they have done from the day I brought them up from Egypt and until this day, and they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and served other gods, so they are doing also to you.
en.B: They are doing to you just what they have always done since the day I brought them up from Egypt: to this very day they have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and served other gods.
en.R: Ever since the day I brought them out of Egypt, they have left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and worshiped other gods. They are still doing it today. Now they are doing the same thing to you.

decisions.choice: according to all ... so also to you: Samuel is treated as Yahweh has been
decisions.reason: The verse compares the two. As the people have treated Yahweh all through their history, so they now treat his prophet. Samuel shares in Yahweh's rejection.

decisions.choice: from the day I brought them up from Egypt until this day: the whole history of Israel
decisions.reason: Yahweh sums up the story since the exodus as one of repeated unfaithfulness, as the book of Judges tells it (Judges 2:11-13; 10:6-14).

decisions.choice: forsaken me and served other gods: abandoned Yahweh for the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: To "serve" a god is to worship it. These are the words used for Israel's sin throughout Judges (Judges 2:12-13; 10:13).

decisions.choice: They are doing to you just what they have always done
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the main point, what the people are doing to Samuel, first, and then gives the history it is compared with.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקוֹלָ֑ם אַ֗ךְ כִּֽי־הָעֵ֤ד תָּעִיד֙ בָּהֶ֔ם וְהִגַּדְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם מִשְׁפַּ֣ט הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִמְלֹ֖ךְ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And now listen to their voice; only surely warn you will warn them and tell to them [the] way of the king who will reign over them.

en.L: And now, listen to their voice. Only you shall solemnly warn them, and you shall tell them the way of the king who will reign over them."
en.B: So now, do as they ask. But you must warn them solemnly and tell them the ways of the king who will reign over them."
en.R: So do what they ask. But warn them strongly. Tell them how the king who rules over them will treat them."

decisions.choice: the way of the king: what a king will regularly do and claim as his due
decisions.reason: The word usually means judgment or justice (verse 3), or a ruling or law. But it can also mean the regular practice of a group, as in "the way of the priests" in 2:13, which also describes taking from the people by force. What Samuel goes on to describe (verses 11-17) is not a law that limits the king but what kings will do: take, again and again. So the sense is the king's practice, the demands he will make as if by right. Some take the phrase as "the rights of the king", a formal statement of his powers; Samuel does later write down "the way of the kingdom" in a book (10:25), which may be such a charter. The word also carries irony: Samuel's sons twisted justice, and the king's "justice" will be taking.

decisions.choice: the king who will reign over them: set against the law of the king in Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 17:14-20 sets limits on Israel's king: he must not gather many horses, many wives, or much silver and gold for himself, and he is to read the law all his life so that he does not raise himself above his fellow Israelites. Samuel's warning describes a king with none of those limits, who takes for himself (verses 11-17).

decisions.choice: only ... surely warn: permission with a solemn condition
decisions.reason: "Only" limits what Yahweh has just allowed. The verb "warn" is doubled for emphasis; it means to warn formally, as a witness who can later be pointed to (Deuteronomy 8:19; 1 Kings 2:42).

decisions.choice: the way of the king (Literal); the ways of the king (Balanced); how the king ... will treat them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for the one Hebrew noun; Balanced uses the plural, since a list of practices follows; Readable says what the phrase means for the people. The same choice is made in verse 11.

decisions.choice: do as they ask
decisions.reason: As in verse 7, "listen to their voice" means to grant their request.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֶל־הָעָ֕ם הַשֹּׁאֲלִ֥ים מֵאִתּ֖וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Samuel all [the] words of Yahweh to the people, the [ones] asking from him a king.

en.L: And Samuel spoke all the words of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the people who were asking him for a king.
en.B: So Samuel told the people who were asking him for a king all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.
en.R: Samuel told the people everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said. They were the ones asking him for a king.

decisions.choice: asking for a king: the verb behind the name Saul
decisions.reason: The verb "ask" is the root of the name Saul, which means "asked for". The people's asking points ahead to the king they will be given (9:2; 12:13, 17).

decisions.choice: all the words of Yahweh: Yahweh's whole answer
decisions.reason: Samuel passes on everything Yahweh said, including that the people have rejected Yahweh as king (verse 7), before giving the warning Yahweh commanded (verse 9).

decisions.choice: They were the ones asking him for a king.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the description of the people a sentence of its own.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר זֶ֗ה יִֽהְיֶה֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣ט הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִמְלֹ֖ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֣ם יִקָּ֗ח וְשָׂ֥ם לוֹ֙ בְּמֶרְכַּבְתּ֣וֹ וּבְפָרָשָׁ֔יו וְרָצ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י מֶרְכַּבְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, This will be [the] way of the king who will reign over you: your sons he will take and appoint for himself in his chariot[s] and among his horsemen, and they will run before his chariot[s],

en.L: And he said, "This will be the way of the king who will reign over you: your sons he will take and set [them] for himself in his chariots and among his horsemen, and they will run before his chariots,
en.B: He said, "These will be the ways of the king who will reign over you: your sons he will take and put to work for himself in his chariots and among his horsemen, and they will run in front of his chariots,
en.R: He said, "This is how the king who rules over you will treat you. He will take your sons and make them serve him. Some will drive his chariots or ride his horses. Others will run in front of his chariots.

decisions.choice: the way of the king: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: What follows is the king's practice, the demands he will make as if by right. See verse 9.

decisions.choice: he will take: the key word of Samuel's speech
decisions.reason: The verb "take" comes again and again (verses 11, 13, 14, 16), and "take a tenth" twice more (verses 15, 17). The king the people want is above all one who takes. The list moves from their sons and daughters to their land, their harvest, their servants and animals, and at last to the people themselves (verse 17).

decisions.choice: chariots, horsemen and runners: a standing royal army and guard
decisions.reason: Chariots and horses were the costly core of a king's army, the very thing Deuteronomy 17:16 tells Israel's king not to multiply. Men running ahead of a king's chariot were a sign of royal rank (2 Samuel 15:1; 1 Kings 1:5). The word for chariot is singular in Hebrew but stands for the king's whole chariot force.

decisions.choice: put to work for himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the king will "set them for himself" in his chariots. Balanced makes clear that this is service the king requires of them.

decisions.choice: Some will drive his chariots or ride his horses.
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long Hebrew sentence into short ones and says what the sons will do with the chariots and horses.

source.text: וְלָשׂ֣וּם ל֔וֹ שָׂרֵ֥י אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י חֲמִשִּׁ֑ים וְלַחֲרֹ֤שׁ חֲרִישׁוֹ֙ וְלִקְצֹ֣ר קְצִיר֔וֹ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כְּלֵֽי־מִלְחַמְתּ֖וֹ וּכְלֵ֥י רִכְבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and to appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and to plow his plowing and to reap his harvest, and to make weapons of his war and [the] equipment of his chariot[s].

en.L: and to set for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and to plow his plowing and to reap his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment of his chariots.
en.B: and he will appoint some for himself as commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and others to plow his fields and reap his harvest and make his weapons of war and the equipment for his chariots.
en.R: He will make some of them army officers, in charge of a thousand men or fifty men. He will make others plow his fields and bring in his harvest. Others will have to make weapons for his army and parts for his chariots.

decisions.choice: commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties: officers over army units
decisions.reason: The army was organized in units under their commanders (Exodus 18:21; Numbers 31:14; 2 Kings 1:9). "Thousand" may name a unit raised from a clan rather than an exact count (see the note at Numbers 1:21). Saul later asks whether David would make his men "commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds" (22:7).

decisions.choice: plow his plowing and reap his harvest: forced labor on the king's land
decisions.reason: The king will own estates of his own and make free Israelites work them. Solomon later raised forced labor from all Israel (1 Kings 5:27; 12:4).

decisions.choice: weapons of war and the equipment of his chariots: arms and gear made in the king's workshops
decisions.reason: The first phrase names weapons in general; the second the fittings and gear of chariots. The king's war machine will be built by the labor of Israel's sons.

decisions.choice: some ... others
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the tasks one after another. Balanced supplies "some" and "others" to show that the sons will be divided among them.

decisions.choice: army officers, in charge of a thousand men or fifty men
decisions.reason: Readable explains the titles. Like the other levels it keeps the numbers of the Hebrew.

source.text: וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם יִקָּ֑ח לְרַקָּח֥וֹת וּלְטַבָּח֖וֹת וּלְאֹפֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And your daughters he will take for perfumers and for cooks and for bakers.

en.L: And your daughters he will take for perfumers and for cooks and for bakers.
en.B: He will take your daughters to be perfumers and cooks and bakers.
en.R: He will take your daughters to make perfumes for him, and to cook and bake for him.

decisions.choice: perfumers and cooks: women who mixed perfumes and prepared food
decisions.reason: The first word is from the verb for mixing spices and oils, used for making the holy anointing oil and incense (Exodus 30:25, 35). The second can mean cooks or those who slaughter and prepare meat; the related word for a man is used of the cook in 9:23-24.

decisions.choice: your daughters he will take: service in the royal household
decisions.reason: A king's palace needed many workers. Daughters would be taken from their families to serve the court, as sons were taken to serve the army (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: to make perfumes for him, and to cook and bake for him
decisions.reason: Readable turns the names of the tasks into verbs and adds "for him", for whom the work is done.

source.text: וְאֶת־שְׂ֠דֽוֹתֵיכֶם וְאֶת־כַּרְמֵיכֶ֧ם וְזֵיתֵיכֶ֛ם הַטּוֹבִ֖ים יִקָּ֑ח וְנָתַ֖ן לַעֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And your fields and your vineyards and your olive groves, the good [ones], he will take, and give to his servants.

en.L: And your fields and your vineyards and your olive groves, the best [ones], he will take and give to his servants.
en.B: The best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves he will take and hand over to his officials.
en.R: He will take your best fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his officials.

decisions.choice: your fields ... he will take: the family land Yahweh gave
decisions.reason: Each family's land was its inheritance from Yahweh and was not to pass out of the family for good (Leviticus 25:23; Numbers 36:7). A king who takes land breaks that order, as Ahab later did with Naboth's vineyard (1 Kings 21:1-16).

decisions.choice: his servants: the king's courtiers and officers
decisions.reason: Here the word names the men who serve the king at court and in his army. Saul later reminds his men that he is the one who can give them fields and vineyards (22:7).

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The word Literal renders "servants" here means the king's court officials, so Balanced and Readable say "officials", as the term list for these books sets out.

source.text: וְזַרְעֵיכֶ֥ם וְכַרְמֵיכֶ֖ם יַעְשֹׂ֑ר וְנָתַ֥ן לְסָרִיסָ֖יו וְלַעֲבָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And your seeds and your vineyards he will tithe, and give to his eunuchs and to his servants.

en.L: And your grain and your vineyards he will tithe, and give [it] to his eunuchs and to his servants.
en.B: He will take a tenth of your grain and of your grape harvest and give it to his court officials and his servants.
en.R: He will take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officials and servants.

decisions.choice: he will tithe: the king takes a tenth as if it were his own
decisions.reason: The tenth of the land's produce belonged to Yahweh and was given to the Levites, or eaten before Yahweh with the poor (Leviticus 27:30-32; Numbers 18:21; Deuteronomy 14:22-29). The king will claim a tenth for himself.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: royal officials, perhaps castrated men
decisions.reason: The word can mean a man who has been castrated, as palace servants often were in the ancient Near East, or more broadly a high court official. Potiphar, who had a wife, is called by this word (Genesis 37:36; 39:1). Here it most likely names the king's officers in general.

decisions.choice: your seeds: the grain grown from your sowing
decisions.reason: The plural of "seed" here means the crops of the fields, set beside the produce of the vineyards.

decisions.choice: grain; grape harvest (Balanced); court officials and servants
decisions.reason: Literal says "grain" for "seeds" and keeps "vineyards"; Balanced and Readable name what is taken from the vineyards, the grapes. Balanced says "court officials" for the first word and keeps "servants" for the second, so that the two groups stay distinct.

source.text: וְאֶת־עַבְדֵיכֶם֩ וְֽאֶת־שִׁפְח֨וֹתֵיכֶ֜ם וְאֶת־בַּחוּרֵיכֶ֧ם הַטּוֹבִ֛ים וְאֶת־חֲמוֹרֵיכֶ֖ם יִקָּ֑ח וְעָשָׂ֖ה לִמְלַאכְתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And your male slaves and your female slaves and your young men, the good [ones], and your donkeys he will take, and use [them] for his work.

en.L: And your male slaves and your female slaves, and your young men, the best [ones], and your donkeys he will take and put [them] to his work.
en.B: He will take your male and female servants, the best of your young men, and your donkeys, and put them to work for himself.
en.R: He will take your servants, both men and women, and your strongest young men and your donkeys. He will make them all work for him.

decisions.choice: your young men (the Hebrew text)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "your cattle", which in Hebrew differs by one letter and would fit beside "your donkeys". The Hebrew text, "your young men", is kept; it also makes sense in a list of workers, and the meaning of the verse is the same: the king takes labor.

decisions.choice: your male slaves and female slaves: the workers of a household
decisions.reason: Many Israelite households had slaves, owned rather than hired (Exodus 21:2-11). The king will take even them for his own service.

decisions.choice: his work: the king's projects and labor
decisions.reason: The word means work or labor of any kind. It will be used of the king's building works and their forced labor (1 Kings 5:30; 9:23).

decisions.choice: male and female servants
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slaves"; Balanced and Readable say "servants", as the style guide sets out, since the point here is their work, not their slavery.

source.text: צֹאנְכֶ֖ם יַעְשֹׂ֑ר וְאַתֶּ֖ם תִּֽהְיוּ־ל֥וֹ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Your flock he will tithe, and you, you will be to him for slaves.

en.L: Your flocks he will tithe, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
en.B: Of your flocks he will take a tenth, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
en.R: He will take one out of every ten of your sheep and goats. And you yourselves will become his slaves.

decisions.choice: you will become his slaves: back to what Yahweh freed them from
decisions.reason: Yahweh brought Israel out of "the house of slaves" (Exodus 20:2) and said that the Israelites are his own slaves and must not be sold as slaves (Leviticus 25:42). Samuel's list ends where it has been heading: not only their goods but the people themselves will belong to the king.

decisions.choice: you yourselves: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out in addition to the verb, setting the people themselves against the flocks and fields just listed.

decisions.choice: flock: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: The word covers both sheep and goats kept together in one flock.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: Here slavery itself is the point: the warning recalls Israel's slavery in Egypt. So every level keeps "slaves", as the style guide asks where "servant" would change the meaning.

source.text: וּזְעַקְתֶּם֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא מִלִּפְנֵ֣י מַלְכְּכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּ֖ם לָכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־יַעֲנֶ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will cry out in the day that because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, and not will answer Yahweh you in the day that.

en.L: And you will cry out in that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not answer you in that day."
en.B: When that day comes, you will cry out because of the king you have chosen for yourselves, but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not answer you then."
en.R: A day will come when you cry out for help because of the king you chose. But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not answer you."

decisions.choice: you will cry out ... Yahweh will not answer: the pattern of Judges will not hold
decisions.reason: Again and again in Judges, Israel cried out under an oppressor and Yahweh raised up someone to rescue them (Judges 3:9, 15; 6:6-7; 10:10). Israel had cried out in Egypt too (Exodus 2:23). But the oppressor Samuel foresees is a king they have chosen for themselves, and Yahweh will not rescue them from their own choice.

decisions.choice: whom you have chosen for yourselves: set against the king Yahweh chooses
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 17:15 says Israel may set over itself only a king "whom Yahweh your God chooses". Samuel stresses that this king is the people's choice, for themselves.

decisions.choice: in that day ... in that day: the verse is framed by the same phrase
decisions.reason: The repeated "in that day" ties the cry and the silence to one coming time of trouble.

decisions.choice: cry out for help
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Readable adds "for help" to show what kind of crying out this is.

source.text: וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ הָעָ֔ם לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ בְּק֣וֹל שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֹּ֔א כִּ֥י אִם־מֶ֖לֶךְ יִֽהְיֶ֥ה עָלֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But refused the people to listen to [the] voice of Samuel, and they said, No, but a king shall be over us,

en.L: But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said, "No, but a king shall be over us,
en.B: But the people refused to listen to Samuel. "No," they said, "we will have a king over us,
en.R: But the people would not listen to Samuel. They said, "No! We want a king to rule over us.

decisions.choice: refused to listen to the voice of Samuel: would not take his warning
decisions.reason: Yahweh told Samuel to "listen to their voice" (verses 7, 9, 22), but the people will not listen to his. The same phrase marks both sides.

decisions.choice: no, but a king shall be over us: a flat refusal and an insistence
decisions.reason: The people answer with a bare "No" and then the strong "but" that sets their own wish against Samuel's warning. Their sentence runs on into verse 20.

decisions.choice: "No," they said,
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "they said" inside the quotation, after the people's first word, which gives their "No" its force.

source.text: וְהָיִ֥ינוּ גַם־אֲנַ֖חְנוּ כְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּשְׁפָטָ֤נוּ מַלְכֵּ֨נוּ֙ וְיָצָ֣א לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ וְנִלְחַ֖ם אֶת־מִלְחֲמֹתֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and will be also we like all the nations, and will judge us our king and go out before us and fight our battles.

en.L: and we also will be like all the nations, and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles."
en.B: so that we too may be like all the nations. Our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles."
en.R: Then we will be like all the other nations. Our king will lead us. He will go out in front of us and fight our battles for us."

decisions.choice: we also will be like all the nations: the wish of verse 5 restated
decisions.reason: The people repeat their wish, now with "we also" stressed, in the very words Deuteronomy foresaw (Deuteronomy 17:14). It is the opposite of Israel's calling to be different from the nations (Leviticus 20:26).

decisions.choice: fight our battles: they want a warrior king
decisions.reason: Yahweh had fought for Israel (Exodus 14:14; Deuteronomy 1:30), most recently with thunder against the Philistines when Samuel prayed (7:10). The people now want a visible king to lead them in war.

decisions.choice: go out before us: lead us into battle
decisions.reason: To "go out and come in before" the people means to lead them in war (18:16; Numbers 27:17).

decisions.choice: lead us
decisions.reason: Readable says "lead" for "judge", as in verses 1 and 5.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י הָעָ֑ם וַֽיְדַבְּרֵ֖ם בְּאָזְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And heard Samuel all [the] words of the people and spoke them in [the] ears of Yahweh.

en.L: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he spoke them in the ears of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: When Samuel had heard all that the people said, he repeated it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Samuel listened to everything the people said. Then he told {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} all of it.

decisions.choice: spoke them in the ears of Yahweh: told Yahweh directly
decisions.reason: To speak "in the ears of" someone is to say it to them in person. Samuel brings the people's words to Yahweh, as he brought Yahweh's words to the people (verse 10).

decisions.choice: all the words of the people: matching all the words of Yahweh
decisions.reason: Verse 10 said Samuel told the people "all the words of Yahweh"; now he tells Yahweh "all the words of the people". Samuel stands between them as go-between.

decisions.choice: repeated it to (Balanced); told ... all of it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the Hebrew picture "in the ears of".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־שְׁמוּאֵל֙ שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקוֹלָ֔ם וְהִמְלַכְתָּ֥ לָהֶ֖ם מֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶל־אַנְשֵׁ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְעִירֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Samuel, Listen to their voice and make reign for them a king. And said Samuel to [the] men of Israel, Go each man to his city.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Listen to their voice, and make a king reign over them." And Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go, each man to his city."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Samuel, "Do as they ask, and give them a king." Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go back, each of you, to your own town."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told Samuel, "Do what they ask. Give them a king." Then Samuel said to the leaders of Israel, "All of you, go back home to your towns."

decisions.choice: listen to their voice and make a king for them: Yahweh's third command
decisions.reason: For the third time Yahweh tells Samuel to grant the people's request (verses 7, 9). The verb "make reign" comes from the same root as "king".

decisions.choice: the men of Israel ... go each to his city: the elders are sent home
decisions.reason: "The men of Israel" are the elders who came to Ramah (verse 4). Samuel sends them home without naming a king. The story of how Yahweh chooses Saul follows (9:1-10:24).

decisions.choice: city: a town of any size
decisions.reason: The word names any walled settlement, large or small.

decisions.choice: Do as they ask, and give them a king
decisions.reason: As in verses 7 and 9, "listen to their voice" means to grant what they ask. Balanced and Readable say "give them a king" for "make a king reign over them".

decisions.choice: the leaders of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" because the men meant are the elders of verse 4 (see m2).
